initial_requirements: The Gemini observatory needs an integrated software environment for controlling its telescopes and scientific instruments. Observing astronomers should be able to acquire astronomical data and assess its quality without having to manage the low-level details of individual subsystems. The system must support users with different operational responsibilities and provide consistent access to telescope status and observing functions from appropriate local or remote facilities.

slots.value: Session start is allowed only when required setup is complete, needed authorization is in place, and readiness checks for telescope, instrument, and safety status all come back clean. If any critical item is incomplete or the system is in an unsafe or ambiguous state, the start should be held until resolved. Session end is allowed when the current observation is complete, or when an operator needs to stop for safety, failure recovery, or an approved handoff. Controls should stay as consistent as possible throughout the system; if the same action appears in different functions, users should not have to relearn what it means or worry that it behaves differently unless there is a very clear operational reason such as safety interlocks or role restrictions. topics.topic_content: Rules governing who may perform which operations

slots.value: Different users with different operational responsibilities; manual changes are limited to the people responsible for that subsystem, usually the instrument specialist for instrument settings and the telescope operator for telescope-related adjustments. The observing astronomer decides the next observing action based on the science plan and telescope state, while an operator or control system carries it out, enforcing safe and valid step sequences. Support staff and automation handle execution, safety, and coordination with telescope subsystems. Under remote operation, sessions should be more conservative due to less immediate physical oversight: if staffing is reduced or on-site response is delayed, manual changes are limited to pre-authorized actions, with automated safeguards or deferred execution preferred over risky forced adjustments; if direct oversight is lost entirely, nonessential changes are blocked until communication and authority are restored. If a request cannot be expressed cleanly at the observing level, the system should translate it automatically into low-level steps when safe and unambiguous; if it is ambiguous, risky, or requires judgment about telescope or instrument state, it should be routed to an operator; only if it cannot be mapped to a valid observing operation at all should it be rejected as too technical. The observing operator or night operator should take over if the instrument specialist cannot resolve an issue in time. On a typical night, observers should work from one consistent interface, and operators should step in only when a change needs approval, a fault appears, or the sequence has to be paused or recovered. If a required state is not met for an action or command, the system should block it outright and tell the user why; queuing is only acceptable when the operation is explicitly designed to wait for a later state and has been agreed as safe and predictable, and allow-with-warning is too risky except possibly for very low-impact actions.

topics.topic_content: Interface usability for observing astronomers and operators

slots.value: Observing astronomers should be able to acquire scientific data and assess its quality without getting bogged down in low-level instrument and control subsystem mechanics; the workflow should let them point, configure, monitor, and assess the observation through a single reliable interface. The workflow should also keep operational complexity low so time isn’t wasted. They should not have to deal with individual device protocols, hardware registers, timing sequences, or the separate steps needed to move motors, switch filters, or synchronize exposures, and they should be hidden from underlying safety interlocks, network connections, and low-level error recovery for each subsystem. The system should also let observers work from one consistent interface and avoid forcing them to deal with subsystem details when getting ready, loading sequences, acquiring targets, checking data quality, and switching instruments or configurations. New telescope configurations or instruments should use the same observing steps, status model, and operator controls with only added parameters or device-specific translations when possible; if they introduce a different sequence of actions, new timing constraints, or a different way of assessing data quality, they need a dedicated adaptation to preserve the common observing workflow.

slots.key: Protection of operational telemetry and observing data
slots.value: Restrict telemetry or observing data when it could expose sensitive operational details, proprietary observing programs, or access-limited engineering information. In live operations, observers should see the data and status needed for the current session, while data from other programs or restricted technical diagnostics should be masked unless the user is authorized. During a security concern or proprietary period, delay or concealment may be necessary, subject to confirmation of the exact policy with operations and data management. In an active session, operators and the assigned observing team may view live telemetry and the data needed to run the observation only if properly authorized for that program or facility. Copying or exporting is limited to users with the right role and permission, especially for raw data, engineering telemetry, or anything under a proprietary period. If a user is not authorized, or if the information belongs to another program or reveals restricted diagnostics, it should be masked or withheld rather than partially exposed. The default should be to show only the current program's information; cross-program data, deeper diagnostics, or partially restricted details appear only when the user's role explicitly calls for it and they are cleared for that level of access. If there is any doubt, hide it.
